item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Japan Institute of International Affairs --Japan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
01.10.2025JIIA Center for Global Outreach (CGO) Established

发布源: Japan Institute of International Affairs --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

I am Takio Yamada, and it is my honor to assume the position of Executive Director of the newly established Center for Global Outreach (CGO) at The Japan Institute of International Affairs (JIIA).At present, the international community is confronted with profound challenges. Serious conflicts unfolding across multiple regions, the policy directions of the new US administration, the rise of the Global South, and the acceleration of technological innovation are all injecting both fresh dynamism and considerable complexity into global affairs.Against this backdrop of fundamental transformation in the international and regional order, JIIA has recognized the imperative for Japan to engage more actively and constructively in addressing global issues. Drawing upon Japan’s accumulated experience and soft power, JIIA established the CGO on October 1, 2025, with the conviction that Japan can and must play a greater role in fostering solutions.The CGO is dedicated to advancing thought leadership, dialogue, and policy recommendations on pressing global and regional challenges. It will also undertake the proactive dispatch of distinguished Japanese experts overseas, while placing strong emphasis on cultivating the next generation of leaders who will shape the future.In addition, the CGO will harness digital platforms, including social media and online conference broadcasting, to encourage open dialogue and inclusive participation. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在1. National Institute for Educational Policy Research (NIER) --Japan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The delegation from the Arab Republic of Egypt visited NIER.

发布源: 1. National Institute for Educational Policy Research (NIER) --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

On Monday 17 February 2025, the delegation of the Arab Republic of Egypt: Mohamed Ahmed Abdellatif Ramadan Saad, the Minister of Education and Technical Education with the other officials visited the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) and NIER.First, MEXT explained special needs education, ICT education, CBT system, and curriculum revision process in Japan, and they had a discussion on the practice of Japanese-style education at the Egyptian Japanese School (EJS), and then NIER: Ikeda, Director General; Ono, Director of Dept. for the International Research and Co-operation; Sakurai, Head of the Academic Ability Div. at the Curriculum Research Center explained about an international assessment of student performance and the National Assessment of Academic Ability. We also had a lively discussion.

item.content:encoded:
NIER International Symposium on Educational Reform, FY2025 The speaker from Finland has been replaced due to unforeseen circumstances.

发布源: 1. National Institute for Educational Policy Research (NIER) --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

Education policies in countries around the world currently aim to ensure the well-being of children and teachers.This international symposium will therefore invite panelists from the United Kingdom, South Korea and Finland to report on the following: the context in which education policies regarding the well-being of children and teachers are discussed in each country; the scope of well-being to be addressed in schools and the associated initiatives ; and the indicators used to measure well-being and improve these initiatives.A panel discussion with experts from four countries, including Japan, will explore approaches to school reform that enhance the well-being of children and teachers. The discussion aims to build a foundation for research in this field by synthesizing the insights offered by the experts from each country.

Materials※Only the original video data will be posted. Please use the translation function as needed when viewing.

The speaker from Finland has been replaced due to unforeseen circumstances.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在1. National Institute for Educational Policy Research (NIER) --Japan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Departments & Centers

发布源: 1. National Institute for Educational Policy Research (NIER) --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

The Department of Research Planning and Development is responsible for the overall planning and coordination of NIER's research and project activities. It manages the setting of research topics, progress administration, and results reporting such that "project research" can be conducted effectively and efficiently. "Project research" is pursued by cross-organizational teams in response to education policy issues and social demands. The department also works to disseminate the results of NIER's research by organizing symposiums as well as by publishing the NIER bulletin and NIER News.

The Office for Educational Resources Research Promotion publishes and broadly distributes NIER's research findings and various data pertaining to educational practices and research via its database and website. In addition, it houses the Library of Education, which contains approximately 540,000 books including educational literature and materials that serve to support research activities within and outside of NIER. The Office also maintains and manages an information system that is the basis for the entirety of research activities at NIER.

Taking into account historical developments and the outlook for educational policy, the Department for Educational Policy and Evaluation Research carries out empirical and comparative research on issues that form the basis for planning, implementing, and evaluating Japan's national educational policies. 2026.08.18Interview With Professor Nishitateno Shuhei: How Development Cooperation Can Deliver Mutual Benefits

发布源: 33. Japan International Cooperation Agency Research Institute (JICA-RI) --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

Updates from JICA Ogata Research Institute on the latest events, publications and more.

Discussions about the purpose of official development assistance (ODA) have become increasingly active in recent years. Using a wide range of data on trade, infrastructure export and diplomacy,Nishitateno Shuhei, Professor at Kwansei Gakuin University, examines how ODA, which supports the growth of developing countries, also affects Japan as a donor country.Katsurai Taro, Senior Research Fellow, JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute), asked Professor Nishitateno about the background, findings and future directions of his research, particularly from the perspectives of trust and mutual benefit.

Katsurai:First of all, how did you come to study Japanese ODA?

Nishitateno:I actually started focusing on ODA studies fairly recently. In graduate school, I specialized in international trade and supply chains, conducting quantitative analyses of production networks in the automotive industry. My interests later extended to environmental issues and sustainable development through joint research with environmental economists at the Australian National University. After returning to Japan, I joined the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), where I was involved in policymaking and gained a broad perspective on the challenges facing the Japanese economy.

Dracopoulos iDeas Lab

发布源: 66. Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

The Andreas C. Dracopoulos iDeas Lab enhances CSIS's work, reach, and impact with the latest digital media, multimedia, and design

The Andreas C. Dracopoulos iDeas Lab is CSIS's internal innovation incubator. It combines the best of web development, video, audio, and design to communicate policy solutions for the world’s greatest foreign policy and national security challenges to a wide audience.

CSIS is the only think-tank that has in-house web developers, designers, animators, and video and audio producers who create innovative and engaging products in the international policy space. We believe in a cross-disciplinary approach to telling policy stories. Our team's diverse backgrounds and skills bring the best of all types of media together to create original and innovative digital and print experiences.

CSIS experts partner with our producers, designers, and developers to adapt their efforts into a range of compelling products. The videos, podcasts, websites, reports, visualizations, and other products the iDeas Lab creates are all designed to engage our audience and propel policy discourse forward. Our work has accumulated millions of engagements, reaching a global audience in government, the media, industry, and beyond.

Leadership Development

发布源: 56. Tokyo Foundation --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

One of our missions is to identify and nurture leaders of the future, both in Japan and around the world. We undertake fellowship programs to develop outstanding human resources capable of seeing issues from a broad perspective and creatively pursuing the right path, as well as initiatives to support Japanese-language educators and promote a fuller understanding of Japan.

Launched in 1987, the Ryoichi Sasakawa Young Leaders Fellowship Fund (Sylff) is a global fellowship program aimed at nurturing leaders who will initiate action to transcend differences and address issues confronting contemporary society. In addition to offering fellowships to graduate students in the humanities and social sciences at 69 universities in 44 countries, Sylff provides ongoing support to encourage fellows’ career development.https://www.sylff.org

The Nippon Foundation Fund for Japanese Language Education Program (NF-JLEP) was established in 1994 to promote Japanese-language education through the training of Japanese-language teachers, provision of fellowships to students pursuing Japanese-related studies, and development of teaching materials. Endowments of $1.5 million were originally provided to 8 universities in 6 countries; today, the number of NF-JLEP institutions has grown to 10.https://www.nf-jlep.org/en

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在56. Tokyo Foundation --Japan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Important Notice: Fraudulent Documents and Recruitment Scams Using the Tokyo Foundation's Name

发布源: 56. Tokyo Foundation --Japan | 抓取时间: 2026-08-29

NEWSAugust 24, 2026

It has come to our attention that documents bearing the Tokyo Foundation's name, together with the names and signatures of individuals associated with the Foundation, have been produced without authorization and used to solicit individuals for employment or contract work. We have also identified messages sent from addresses outside our official domain, as well as job listings posted in the Foundation's name on recruitment platforms. None of these communications or listings originate from, or are in any way connected to, the Tokyo Foundation.

Please note the following:- The Foundation uses the domain "@tkfd.or.jp" for all of its email addresses. Messages from any other domain are not from us.- English-language job openings are posted on this website. An English-language job listing that does not appear here is not from the Foundation. As of the date of this notice, the Foundation has no open English-language positions.- The Foundation never requests payment of any kind in connection with employment or contract work.

If you receive a communication you do not recognize, please do not reply to it, open any attached files, or provide personal information. If you have already corresponded with the sender, or if you are unsure whether a message claiming to come from the Foundation is genuine, please contact us at the address below. We also encourage you to report the matter to the police or other appropriate authorities.

The Tokyo Foundationinfo@tkfd.or.jp
